slice.name: ambiguous_candidate_create_read_before_retry
slice.objective: Test deterministic recovery after a candidate create returns an ambiguous client result, requiring read-at-K exact-byte reconciliation before any second create or pointer CAS.
slice.model: Finite deterministic state machine over an immutable deterministic candidate key K and exact canonical bytes B. The initial create has one of three client outcomes: confirmed success, confirmed failure-before-commit, or ambiguous failure-after-possible-commit. The ambiguous branch must read K before any further mutation.
protocol: confirmed success: candidate may be adopted; pointer-last CAS is allowed only if the frozen parent LATEST is still current
confirmed failure-before-commit: one retry create is safe because non-commit is known; no further retry occurs in-run if that retry is not confirmed
ambiguous result: read deterministic K first
if K contains exact B: adopt existing candidate and do not create again
if K is absent: issue at most one create; if that create is not confirmed, checkpoint the ambiguity and stop this invocation
if K contains non-B bytes: diagnostic stop; never overwrite
before pointer update in every adoption path: require CAS from the frozen parent; stale parent means diagnostic stop and no pointer mutation

negative_controls.blind_retry_after_ambiguous_exact: FAIL: attempts a second create despite K already containing B, creating duplicate/conflict risk.
negative_controls.overwrite_on_K_mismatch: FAIL: destroys immutable-key collision evidence and can adopt bytes not derived from the frozen semantic payload.
negative_controls.unconditional_pointer_write_after_parent: FAIL: can advance LATEST from a stale parent and adopt an orphaned revision.

slice.verdict: PASS in the tested finite deterministic model. Read-at-K exact-byte reconciliation makes the ambiguous create path idempotent with respect to candidate identity: exact B is adopted without another create, absence permits one create, mismatch stops without overwrite, and pointer-last CAS prevents stale-parent adoption.

comparison.candidate_A: read-at-K exact-byte reconciliation plus parent-guarded pointer-last CAS
comparison.candidate_B: blind retry after ambiguous client failure
comparison.expected_completion_time: A adds one read on the ambiguous branch but avoids duplicate-create recovery; B can create conflict/recovery work when the first create actually committed.
comparison.success_probability: A satisfied all seven deterministic cases and six invariants; B fails the committed-but-ambiguous case by construction.
comparison.conflict_duplication_risk: A low in tested model; B high on ambiguous-after-commit, mismatch, or stale-parent conditions.
comparison.integration_cost: A needs deterministic K, exact byte comparison and one parent CAS; no new executor or paid quota.
comparison.quota_fragility: No finite monthly trial paid quota or richer-mode dependency.

tested_scope: Seven finite deterministic state-machine cases around one immutable candidate key K and canonical bytes B, including exact/absent/mismatch reads and current/stale parent states; three explicit negative controls. Not tested: live connector ambiguity, silent-overwrite transports, concurrent third-party writes between read-at-K and create, noncanonical semantic serialization, or production collision rates.
conflict_check: Used only frozen sanitized controls, own cross_field r176/LATEST state, and a local deterministic state machine. No O/O-derived state, other-worker state/config/receipts, downstream state, legacy research, shared aggregate ledger, scheduler, or protected-primary semantic input was used or mutated.
candidate_revision: After any ambiguous candidate-create result, reconcile deterministic K before retry: exact canonical bytes mean adopt without another create; absent means create at most once; mismatch means diagnostic stop without overwrite; pointer update is last and only via CAS from the frozen parent. A second ambiguous create result is checkpointed rather than retried in-run.
frontier: Test noncanonical semantic serialization defenses so logically identical semantic objects cannot acquire different candidate keys.
Then test concurrent write interleavings between read-at-K absence and create, including create-conflict reconciliation without in-run retry loops.
exact_continuation: Next invocation, bootstrap and freeze authority, read own LATEST r177 only as needed, then execute exactly one bounded noncanonical-semantic-serialization leaf. Build logically identical candidate objects with reordered keys, Unicode normalization variants, numeric edge encodings and omitted/default-field variants; require one canonical byte string/key or an explicit rejection rule, and preserve concurrent read/create interleaving as the following leaf.
